summary: The paper introduces the Classically‑Boosted Quantum Optimization Algorithm (CBQOA), which uses a classical seed solution followed by a continuous‑time quantum walk–based state preparation and a p‑layer variational circuit. Simulations on 100 hard instances of Max‑3SAT (16 variables, 200 clauses) and Max‑Bisection (12‑vertex graphs) show higher probabilities of finding high‑quality solutions compared with the classical seed algorithms and GM‑QAOA at depth p=3. All results are obtained via classical simulation with small problem sizes.

experiments.description: Classically-Boosted Quantum Optimization Algorithm (CBQOA) applied to Max 3SAT, using a Karloff-Zwick classical seed and a gate-based continuous-time quantum walk plus phase-separator layers; evaluated on 100 hard random weighted Max 3SAT instances.

algorithm.ansatz: Alternating layers of e^{-i\beta_j|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|} and e^{-i\gamma_j H_f} after CTQW state preparation
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Not specified; parameters tuned by CVaR minimization

hyperparameters.N: not specified for exact CTQW; exact implementation on Max 3SAT

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Seed state from Karloff-Zwick classical approximation; quantum parameters optimized from unspecified initial values

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One qubit per Boolean variable, with auxiliary variables x0 and x_{n+1}..x_{2n} used in the Max 3SAT formulation; valid assignments encoded as computational basis states
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize total clause weight; equivalently minimize f(x)=\sum_{(i,j,k)\in C} w_{i,j,k}[(1-x_i)(1-x_j)(1-x_k)-1]
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Unconstrained formulation via auxiliary variables; CBQOA keeps evolution in feasible subspace by construction

problem_instance.description: 100 hard weighted Max 3SAT instances with 16 variables and 200 clauses each

dataset_specification.description: Instances generated with 16 variables, 200 clauses, clause weights uniformly random in [0,1]; hard instances selected by low POGS_0.7 for Karloff-Zwick

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Generate random instance; solve SDP relaxation; perform random hyperplane rounding 10000 times; keep instances with estimated POGS_0.7(KZ)<0.05
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 100 hard instances; compare POGS thresholds over repeated simulations; 10000 rounding samples used to estimate classical seed quality

implementation_details.classical_solver: Karloff–Zwick SDP relaxation followed by Goemans–Williamson–style random hyperplane rounding
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical SDP relaxation to generate seed; CTQW weights set from seed neighborhood; CVaR-based parameter tuning
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure computational basis and evaluate approximation ratio / POGS

speedup_claims.conditions: 100 hard weighted Max 3SAT instances; p=3; alpha=0.5; Orquestra simulation
speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit numeric improvement factor reported; claim is based on histogram comparisons of POGS thresholds.

speedup_claims.conditions: Exact CTQW and phase separators under the stated assumptions
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a complexity statement, not an empirical speedup; no asymptotic advantage over classical algorithms is proven.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical SDP for seed generation in ~O((|C|+n)^{3.5}) time; best-known classical for Max 3SAT not characterized here

limiting_factors: No runtime comparison against classical heuristics
Results reported only as probability-of-good-solution histograms

circuit_depth not explicitly reported for Max 3SAT; only the CTQW is said to be implemented exactly and the overall circuit uses p=3 layers.

experiments.description: Classically-Boosted Quantum Optimization Algorithm (CBQOA) applied to Max Bisection, using a Feige-Langberg classical seed and a gate-based XY-mixer-style continuous-time quantum walk; evaluated on 100 hard random weighted Max Bisection instances.

algorithm.ansatz: Alternating layers of e^{-i\beta_j|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|} and e^{-i\gamma_j H_f} after CTQW state preparation
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Not specified; parameters tuned by CVaR minimization
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Seed state from Feige-Langberg classical approximation; quantum parameters optimized from unspecified initial values

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One qubit per vertex; feasible solutions are n-bit strings of Hamming weight n/2 representing bisections
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize cut weight subject to |S|=n/2; f(x)=\sum_{(a,b)\in E} w_{a,b}(2x_ax_b-x_a-x_b)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Feasible-subspace-preserving CTQW on bisection states; no penalty terms

problem_instance.description: 100 hard Max Bisection instances on random weighted graphs

dataset_specification.description: Erdős-Rényi graphs G(n,p) with n=12, p=0.5; edge weights uniformly random in [-1,1]; hard instances selected by low POGS_0.99 for Feige-Langberg

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Generate random graph; solve SDP relaxation; perform RPR2 rounding 10000 times; keep instances with estimated POGS_0.99(FL)<0.05
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 100 hard instances; compare POGS thresholds over repeated simulations; 10000 rounding samples used to estimate classical seed quality

implementation_details.classical_solver: Feige–Langberg SDP relaxation followed by RPR2 randomized projection rounding
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical SDP relaxation to generate seed; CTQW weights set from seed neighborhood; CVaR-based parameter tuning
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure computational basis and evaluate approximation ratio / POGS

speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit numeric improvement factor reported; claim is based on histogram comparisons of POGS thresholds.
